t: You're standing in Dean's Yard, a large gated quadrangle that makes up most of what remains of the old monastery precincts of Westminster Abbey. It's closed to traffic, and the central green is where Westminster School pupils, who simply call it Green, have long had the right to sit, read and play football. Church House stands to the south. The architect William Samwell was born here in 1628, and Sir Walter Tapper, an architect of churches who became Surveyor of the Fabric of Westminster Abbey, died here in 1935.
